rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig`. The subject says the type overrides the OpenAI model, endpoint, credentials and inference options, and that omitted settings use the defaults in the agent configuration contract. It also fixes the struct shape, the builder methods and the trait set. The defaults come from `agent_config.settings`: `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and the option defaults the tests check. I read the supplied tests only. I did not request implementation source.

**Mapping obligations to tests (all in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs`, `mod[tests]`, unless noted)**
- **Field shape and builders** (`new`, `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key`, `option`): `fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` asserts `OpenAiConfig::new()` serializes to `{}`. It then applies every builder and asserts the exact serialized object: model, endpoint, api_key_env, api_key and options `{"a":2}`.
- **Serde and `PartialEq`**: `fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` deserializes an OpenAI config with model, endpoint, api_key and nested options. It asserts that re-serializing gives the same JSON and that the value survives a string round trip with `assert_eq!` on `PartialEq`. `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` asserts that `{"backend":"openai"}` deserializes to `OpenAiConfig::new()`, which covers omitted fields.
- **Defaults for omitted settings**: `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts the default model `gpt-6.1-sol`, the default endpoint, and the default options (`max_output_tokens` 16384, `reasoning.effort` "low"). `fn[openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable]` re-runs itself in a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. It asserts that `resolved_api_key` returns that value, which covers the default credential variable.
- **Overriding options**: `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` sets `max_output_tokens` to 42 and gets 42. It also checks that `reasoning` `{"summary":"auto"}` gets the default effort filled in, and that an explicit `effort: "high"` is kept.
- **Overriding credentials**: `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` shows that an unset `api_key_env` produces an error naming the variable. It also shows that an explicit `api_key` resolves to the explicit value even when the named environment variable is absent.
- **Overriding model and endpoint in use**: `fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs` sets a custom model, endpoint and api_key. A local server checks that requests go to the custom endpoint and carry model `local-test`. They also carry the default `max_output_tokens` of 16384. The test also asserts that the saved evidence does not contain the key or model.
- **`Clone` and `Debug`**: these are standard trait implementations that add no behavior beyond the listed obligations. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs` `fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public export inventory.

**Considered and not treated as a gap**
- Replacing a repeated `option` key is stated in `agent_config.settings`, not in the subject text. It is asserted for the Bedrock builder only. `OpenAiConfig.options` is a `BTreeMap`, and the subject text does not mention replacement, so I do not count this as a gap.
- `SecretString` redaction in `Debug` belongs to another requirement.

No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply.

text: Overrides the SDK’s OpenAI model, endpoint, credentials, or inference options. Omitted settings use the defaults in the agent configuration contract.
pub fn model(self, model: String) -> Self;
pub fn endpoint(self, endpoint: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self;
pub fn option(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self;
TBV exposes configuration for its supplied Bedrock, OpenAI, and Ollama
agents. The configuration selects a backend and carries its model, connection,
`AgentConfig` and its backend-specific configuration types implement Serde
serialization and deserialization. An application can embed them in its own
configuration types; serializing and deserializing a supported configuration
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.
All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.
